doc.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022

title: The mellophone band
summary: Mellophones were out of tune and loud, and Kenton dropped them for cost.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It was part of the sound of the band. One of the things that they did do one time, you know because back with the mellophone band with the Kenton band, those mellophones were out of tune. They were not great instruments. And there had been a mellophonium before with Conn but Johnny Richards and Stan went to Conn and I think the mellophoniums were in E flat but Johnny Richards wanted them in F and they fiddled with them and so the sound was amazing but they were not really very well in tune. And boy those guys had to work. And of course they were so loud. I mean they were louder than the trumpets or the trombones. So people were always trying to get rid of the mellophones and at one point I guess some of them ended up in a swimming pool in a motel. But that’s not — the reason Stan stopped — the mellophone band I think only

went about 3-1/2 years. And it was basically the same as people ask me well with the Kenton Legacy Orchestra how come you don’t have mellophones? Same reason Stan had to get rid of them. I’ve got to pay four more guys? Where am I going to get the money?
